assertion: While China is on track to hit its soybean target, it bought just $7.2 billion worth of the other agricultural goods — from meat to corn — between January and September, the analysis showed. Imports are at their lowest for this period since 2019, at the height of the first trade war.
reason: Matches the Reuters text as republished; Reuters original unreadable (401). econ.trade_exports ends 2025, so Jan-Sep 2026 cannot be checked; its Jan-Sep 2019-2025 US-export values ($3.6B, $9.1B, $7.8B, $4.2B) are a different basis (Census US exports, not Chinese customs imports) and neither confirm nor contradict it.
measure: monthly US goods exports by HS-6 commodity and destination country
warehouse_value: Jan-Sep US exports to China, HS 01-24 excl. soybeans: 2019 $3.58B, 2023 $9.08B, 2024 $7.82B, 2025 $4.21B; 2026 not loaded
sql: SELECT year, SUM(value_usd)/1e9 FROM econ.trade_exports WHERE geo_level='country' AND country_name ILIKE 'China%' AND hs2 IN ('01'..'24') AND hs6 NOT LIKE '1201%' AND CAST(month AS INTEGER)<=9 GROUP BY year
